Subject: RE: Redwood POC — cost sanity & MAP items

Looping in initial econ thoughts so we have something concrete on the call: 

Quick assumptions (ballpark, to be replaced with Helix profile):
- Average request size: 1.8k prompt tokens + 400 response tokens (2.2k total)
- Baseline tokens/$ on hosted variants (mixed open models): ~40k tokens per $ (varies by model/quant)
- Target for pilot: net tokens/$ >= 55k by using 1) prefix caching for static instructions (expected 30-50% token reduction for certain flows) and 2) batching for high-concurrency endpoints (improve utilization; expect 15-25% effective cost improvement under 50ms batching windows)

Proposed checks to include in MAP:
- Cacheable traffic fraction (customer to provide request traces): we need an estimate of how many requests share identical prefixes or instruction sets.
- Typical sequence lengths distribution (P50/P90/P99) — drives kernel selection and token cost.
- Concurrency profile by route — to size batching windows and reserved capacity.
- Acceptance criterion: pilot must demonstrate tokens/$ improvement of at least 20% vs baseline within first 2 weeks OR model-switch policy to a cheaper variant with equivalent quality.

I will bring a short worksheet on the call that turns their CSV into expected tokens/$ under different caching/hit-rate scenarios.

—Karthik
Head of Inference Economics

Attachment: redwood_cost_notes.pdf (summary of assumptions)

Adding evaluation plan milestones and close timeline — short bullets to include in the MAP: 

Mutual Action Plan (proposed):
- Week 0 (agreement signed): exchange traffic sample + HubSpot doc access
- Week 1 (pilot kickoff): Redwood to run baseline with no caching/vanilla configs; measurement window = 72h
- Week 2 (optimization window): enable prefix caching and recommended batching; measure tokens/$ and latency impact
- Week 3 (evaluation): compare to acceptance criteria; propose rollout plan or next steps (expand pilot or model variant)
- Procurement/legal parallel: aim to finalize SOW and PO by end of Week 2 to avoid procurement gating after success

Evaluation deliverables we will own:
- Token-per-request dashboard (P50/P90 distributions)
- Caching hit-rate estimation and its token-savings delta
- Suggested batching policy per route (target latency SLOs included)

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- Net tokens/$ improvement >= 20% vs baseline OR
- Maintained quality (f1/accuracy or manual review sample) while achieving cost target

I can draft the MAP doc with these milestones after the call — will aim to have v1 by 4/17 EOD.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager
